newsitem.title: BELGIUM: W.Europe air delays increase in Q2 1996 - industry.
newsitem.headline: W.Europe air delays increase in Q2 1996 - industry.

text.p: West European airlines faced more delays in the second quarter of 1996 compared to the same time last year, with 17.4 percent of flights delayed more than 15 minutes, said the Association of European Airlines.
The figure for April-June 1995 was 16.8 percent, according to a Tuesday statement by the AEA, whose members include all the region's major flag carriers.

"Delays reported with airport or air traffic control (ATC) as a primary cause accounted for two-thirds of late departures in April-June, a slightly higher proportion than in 1995. Those attributed to airline-related reasons were down slightly to 5.5 percent of all departures, the best quarterly result for two years," the statement said.

"While ATC delays arising from problems coordinating en-route flight paths are affecting many more flights this year, those relating to movements in the departure and arrival phases of the flight were showing an improvement through the early summer," it said.
